newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge probes Bouygues, TF1 chiefs.
newsitem.headline: French judge probes Bouygues, TF1 chiefs.

text.p: The chairmen of French construction giant Bouygues and private television channel TF1 were placed under judicial investigation on Thursday in a probe into alleged political kickbacks, justice sources said.
A spokesman for Bouygues said chairman Martin Bouygues and three other executives under investigation would be able to continue doing their jobs under the terms of their judicial control.

Bouygues, France's biggest construction and public works company, holds the operating licence for TF1, whose chairman is Patrick Le Lay. The other two men placed under investigation were Bouygues executives Philippe Chalendon and Bernard Devalan.

Judge Jean-Marie Charpier is investigating some five million francs ($880,000) worth of allegedly false invoices made out by Cerail consultancy firm for subsidiaries of Bouygues including Saur, TF1, Bouygues Offshore and Bouygues Diversifications.
The investigative weekly Le Canard Enchaine said the judge suspected the consultancy firm was a front for covert payments to conservative political parties.

All four executives, placed under investigation on suspicion of misuse of corporate funds, were released after questioning by Charpier on condition that they did not make contact the head of Cerail, the justice sources said.
